visual_text: Longer waits for a bed were linked with more deaths
Over 5 million people admitted, England, 2016 to 2018
From 5 hours after arrival up to 12 hours, the longer the wait, the higher the 30-day risk. A link, not proof of cause.
Jones et al., Emerg Med J 2022
The '1 extra death in 82' figure: what it allowed for
Authors' estimate for people delayed beyond 6 to 8 hours
Observed deaths compared with deaths the researchers' model expected.
Allowed for: age, sex, deprivation, long-term conditions, time of day, month, earlier visits, crowding
Not in the model: how ill each person was on arrival
Jones et al., Emerg Med J 2022
In one department, older people's visits lasted longer
Visits lasting 4 hours or more, one English department, 2019
Some of the time is tests and assessment, not only waiting for a bed. Visits, not people.
alt_text: Card 1: over 5 million people admitted in England 2016 to 2018; from 5 to 12 hours of waiting the longer the wait the higher the 30-day death risk, a link not proof of cause. About 9 in 100 died within 30 days. An arrow runs from 5 hours to 12 hours.
Card 2: the 1 extra death in 82 estimate allowed for age, sex, deprivation, long-term conditions, time, month, earlier visits and crowding, but not how ill each person was on arrival.
Card 3: bar chart of visits lasting 4 hours or more in one English department in 2019, per 100 visits: 44 aged 18 to 64, 63 aged 65 to 74, 71 aged 75 to 84, 79 aged 85 and over.
design_instructions: Three 4:5 light cards. Card 1 h1.m, arrow axis 5 hours to 12 hours, mint stat panel (no plotted mortality). Card 2 mint panel with tick icon (Allowed for) and dashed white panel with cross icon (Not in the model). Card 3 custom SVG vertical bars 0 to 100 graded teal. Claims C15-14-a, C15-14-c, C15-14-e.
